subject: USCIS form editions and filing fees
why_this_lane_and_not_a_wider_one: docs/EXTERNAL-AUTHORITY-PLAN.md, Rank 4: 'Pick one narrow lane and hold it --
immigration form and fee changes is the strongest candidate.'
A changelog across five agencies is a worse asset than a changelog across one,
for a reason that is structural rather than editorial. The thing a journalist
cites is 'the record that has watched this page every week since 2026'. That
record is only worth citing if it is unbroken. Every additional agency adds
another page that can move its URL, another fetch that can fail, and another
week where the changelog is partially blind while still publishing. Depth is
the product; breadth is the thing that destroys it.
USCIS form and fee changes were chosen over the alternatives because:
- they change on a real cadence (edition dates, fee rules) rather than never;
- the primary source is a stable federal URL, not a state board PDF that
- Professional Resource Library already carries the immigration surface
(uscis-medical-exam-resources.html and its cost page), so the changelog
lands next to material it actually relates to;
- the affected reader is specific and currently unserved: someone mid-filing
who needs to know whether the edition they downloaded is still accepted.
boundary: This lane reports WHAT CHANGED on a government page and WHEN it was observed.
It does not tell anyone what to do about it, which edition to file, or whether
they qualify for anything. That boundary is the publication's, not this file's:
data/publications.json 'professional' says the publication is educational only
and does not provide professional advice.
